findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee used their bare hands to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed chicken that was cooked yesterday in the cookline cooler was not date marked. During the inspection the chicken was properly date marked. The PIC was reminded that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was prepared/opened being day one). Ensure that required foods are always properly date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following require cleaning:

(1) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The accumulation of dust on the hood system.

(2) The debris on the top of the dish machine. 
 
Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed the following in the cookline single cooler lacked date marking: (1) Chicken that was cooked on Friday; and (2) Jug of milk that was opened on Friday. The chicken was date marked and the milk was discarded during the inspection. The PIC was reminded that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was prepared/opened being day one). Ensure that required foods are always properly date marked.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the hood system has an accumulation of dust. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the hood system is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed the containers holding sugar, salt, and cracker meal were not labeled. All foods not in their original container that can be easily mistakably recognized (ex. white powders) must be identified with the common name. The PIC labeled the containers of salt, sugar, and cracker meal during the inspection. Ensure that all easily mistakable foods not in their original packages are labeled with the common name of the food.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the table holding the coffee machine (to the left of the dish machine) is not sealed to the wall. Since the coffee machinery is attached to the wall the table cannot be easily pulled out for cleaning. The PIC was instructed to seal the surface using caulking or another method. Ensure that the table holding the coffee machines is sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the floors underneath the fryers and grill have an accumulation of grease and food debris. The PIC was instructed to pull out the equipment and clean underneath. An employee began the process of cleaning during the inspection. Ensure that the floors under the fryers and grill are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Quat sanitizer bucket was observed with less than 100ppm quat. CORRECTED- PIC remade the sanitizer bucket, which was then observed at 200ppm. Use test strips to monitor sanitizer concentration.
4-501.114: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label (200-400 ppm). [P]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a knife stored underneath a plastic wrap box at the cook line. In-use utensils must be stored in clean, sanitized locations when in use. Ensure that all utensils are stored properly at the next routine inspection. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The dish machine counter and coffee counter are not easily movable and too close to the wall to be easily moved for cleaning. As such, these areas must be caulked or otherwise sealed to the wall to make these surfaces smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that all surfaces within the facility are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The facility is in need of a thorough deep cleaning. Most hard-to-reach areas have an accumulation of residue and debris. Ensure that a deep cleaning is performed by the next routine inspection and that the facility is free of accumulations of residue/debris. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed foods in the upright to the right of the prep counter to be held at temperatures between 41 and 45 degrees. The internal thermometer and built-in thermostat read 44 degrees F. The acceptable range as shown on the cooler temperature gauge is between 35 and 41 degrees F. Maintenance has been called to fix this. Foods must be stored below 41 degrees. No foods in this cooler were at or below 41 degrees F. The maximum food temperature was 45 degrees. No foods were discarded. Operator instructed to move foods from cooler if the cooler cannot be fixed rapidly. Ensure that foods are held at proper temperatures at all times. A follow-up is issued for 12/12/2022 to verify the cooler has been repaired and is operating within parameters. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several foods in the walk-in cooler which did not have any date marking but were opened and/or prepared. Ensure that all prepared and opened containers of food are date marked as required and discarded within the 7-day period of time for TCS foods. No foods within the walk-in coolers were out of temperature or appeared to be spoiled. Facility will use items without date marking immediately and will label foods in the walk-in cooler. Items without date marking included but were not limited to cheese, prepared fruit, mayonnaise, and cut lettuce. Ensure that date marking is occurring as required. A follow-up is being issued for the 12/19/2022 to ensure proper date marking. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
The person in charge has an expired CFM certificate that expired on March 28, 2022. PIC stated that she thought it was valid until the 28th of this month. Anyone in charge during operational times must have a valid CFM certificate to oversee food preparation. Ensure that valid certificate is obtained prior to next routine inspection in 2022. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed coffee residue in a hand washing sink on east side of the buffet line. The hand sink is in close proximity to the coffee preparation area. Another hand sink is available on the other side but does not have a sign. Recommended to operator that handwashing sink on the other side is the designated sink to allow dumping in the one on the east side. Ensure that hand washing sinks are only used for handwashing.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed chicken in the walk-in freezer sitting on the same shelf and touching pork on the same shelf. Chicken must be stored below pork in the freezer. PIC moved the pork off the shelf. Corrected on site. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Bottles of water were observed to be stored at the base of the rear upright sitting in water from a leak in the cooler. Move the bottles to prevent contamination.

3-303.12: (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if FOOD is subject to entry of water. (B) unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole raw produce, cut, raw vegetables such as celery, carrots, potatoes, or tofu can be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH received in ice may remain in condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Several areas throughout the facility are beginning to accumulate dust, berries and residue. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are cleaned prior to the next routine inspection. Areas of specific concern include but are not limited to:
- the cabinet with the mixer in it underneath the prep station was observed to have debris at the base of it
- floors around the fryers are accumulating oil and other debris
- prep sinks in the less-used portion of the facility are soiled with residue and need to be deep cleaned
- power boxes and disposals under sinks are observed to have a buildup of residue

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Observed the quat sani bucket to be on the top surface of the prep table sitting next to bacon. Ensure sani buckets are stored below food and food contact surfaces to avoid food contamination. The sani bucket was moved to the bottom shelf during the inspection. 
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the mop stored inside the mop bucket in a position that did not allow it to air dry properly. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to air dry properly. Mop was moved during the inspection. 
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
